## 9bdb9da260e9

**Reproduced validator/generator defect.** The public advertised override
`generate(0, 0, texture="missing_match")` emits the task's own documented
`missing_match` degenerate, yet `self_check` returns `[]`. Applying the pinned
canonical rule to that accepted grid then crashes with `hash-ref ... given: #f`
because the gray target shape has no legend match. This can admit a generated
input with no valid label rather than merely leaving a plausible shortcut.

Evidence: `checks/audit/9bdb9da260e9/probe.json`,
`checks/audit/9bdb9da260e9/missing_match_input.json`, and
`checks/audit/9bdb9da260e9/racket.json`. The supported replay command ran from
`repo` and recorded generator SHA-256
`01734793c2824eafff4d34861322ca132c7271163032177713098ec81a0eedf4` and rule
hash `b92199a85bf9`; it exited 1 exactly on the reference crash. The standalone
lint also reports the missing `RULE_HASH` and two unprobeable singleton axes in
`checks/audit/9bdb9da260e9/lint-after/`. No audit-target source was changed.

## 9bdb9da260e9

**Reproduced validator/generator defect.** The advertised call
`generate(0, 0, texture="missing_match")` returns a 12×15 input that
`self_check` accepts with `[]`, even though the gray target shape has no matching
legend shape. The pinned canonical Racket rule then exits 1 with
`hash-ref: contract violation ... given: #f`, so the accepted generator domain
contains an input with no valid output label.

Fresh evidence is in `checks/audit/9bdb9da260e9/probe.json`,
`missing_match_input.json`, and `racket.json`; command stdout/stderr and exit
status are retained beside them. The audited generator SHA-256 is
`01734793c2824eafff4d34861322ca132c7271163032177713098ec81a0eedf4`, and the
executed canonical rule hash is `b92199a85bf9`. This independently reproduces a
prior unresolved audit finding on the same current source. No audit-target
source was changed.
